speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. To help me understand your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That knee pain sounds significant; was it red or warm to the touch, and did you notice any similar rash on your body besides the wrist? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, and CRP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL, Platelets: 300,000 /μL; ESR: Normal Readings; CRP: Normal Readings

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your elevated white blood cell count and recent camping trip to Minnesota, have you noticed any joint swelling or warmth in your left wrist or knee since returning? Did anyone else in your camp get sick, and do you recall any specific insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis) with erythema migrans-like or secondary skin lesions.
